The Katsina State Government has inaugurated 1,008 forest guards to strengthen security in forest reserves and tackle the activities of bandits, terrorists, cattle rustlers and illegal tree fellers. Governor Dikko Radda made this known on Friday during the graduation and passing-out ceremony of the forest guards in Katsina. He charged them to discharge their duties diligently and serve as worthy ambassadors of the country and the communities they represent. According to him, “the forest guards would work in collaboration with about 3,000 members of the state-owned Community Watch Corps, the Civilian Joint Task Force, vigilantes and hunters to secure forests and other security-prone areas across the state”. The governor assured the personnel that his administration would provide the necessary equipment and support to enable them to perform their responsibilities effectively. Radda, however, highlighted measures introduced by his administration, including the establishment of the Community Watch Corps and support for conventional security agencies, which had contributed significantly to reducing banditry and terrorism across the state. He commended President Bola Tinubu for initiating the establishment of forest guards in several states, describing the initiative as a major step towards securing the country’s forest areas. Ribadu, who was represented by a former Assistant Director of the Department of State Services, I.O. Shotoyo, charged the guards to uphold discipline, professionalism and respect for human rights in the discharge of their duties. “The nation counts on you. We expect you to serve with courage, discipline and integrity such that you will be able to reclaim every inch of our forests,” he said. Earlier, the forest guards’ trainer, Lt. Col. George Agar, disclosed that the 1,008 personnel comprised 990 men and 18 women, who underwent eight weeks of intensive training. He said the training covered various combat situations, including the handling of AK-47 rifles, intelligence gathering, night operations, confronting suspected terrorists, rescuing abducted persons and preventing illegal tree felling. Agar expressed confidence that the training had equipped the personnel with the necessary skills to confront security threats and protect forest reserves. The personnel were largely recruited from communities around forest areas affected by insecurity and are expected to commence operations immediately. Esha Aliku
